questions.stem: State the impact of constant mechanical agitation and pumping of air in the aeration tank on the sewage during the biological treatment.

(a) Cattle excreta is important source for producing a domestic fuel. Name the fuel and write its main components.
(b) Write the biological process that is responsible for the production of this fuel.
Mention the two types of acquired immune responses present in our body. Give one major role of each.
questions._flag: Ordinary marking latitude, not a void: the scheme accepts two readings separated by '//', either humoral (antibody-mediated) and cell-mediated immune responses, or primary and secondary immune responses. The solution teaches humoral and cell-mediated (the NCERT pair named for the two types) and names the primary/secondary pair as the scheme's accepted alternative.

questions.stem:
The histogram given below representing the data for annual shark harvest in the great barrier reef / coral reef located on the east coast of Queensland, Australia. Study the histogram and answer the questions that follow.
(a) Write your interpretation of the data given.
(b) Write the impact on the biodiversity of the area that you can interpret on the basis of given data.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a histogram of Catch (tonnes), axis 0 to 1200 in steps of 200, with one bar for each year from 1992 to 2002 on an axis ticked 1992 to 2003, and the caption 'Source : Fijisharkdiving.blogspot.com'; the bar heights carry the trend the question asks the student to interpret, so they are withheld here. Page idx 4.

questions.stem: "Stability of community depends upon its species richness." How did David Tilman show this experimentally ?
Name the source organism (scientific name) that produces statins. Mention its use in medical field and how does it act.

(a) Give an example of viral biocontrol agent.
(b) Why are they considered to be desirable when an ecologically sensitive area is being treated ?

Study the graph given below, showing the population growth curves 'A' and 'B' respectively. Answer the following questions :
(a) What is 'Carrying Capacity' in respect of Curve 'B' indicative of ?
(b) Mention the action of possible natural forces that could have lead to curve 'B'.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a graph of Population size (y) against Time / Generation (x) with a dashed horizontal line marked Carrying Capacity and two curves labelled 'A' and 'B' rising from the origin, the region between them shaded; which curve has which shape (and so which growth model each is) is decided by the drawing and is withheld here. Page idx 6.

questions.stem:
(a) What does the equation \(dN/dt = rN\) express in terms of population growth ?
(b) Write the significance of 'r' in a population survey.

(i) State the role of a selectable marker in r-DNA technology.
(ii) Name one such selectable marker which is considered to be useful for E.coli.
(iii) Give one reason why is it considered to be a useful marker.
What are plasmids ? How are they different from cloning vectors ? Give one example each for a viral and a bacterial cloning vector.
Explain giving reason the action plan followed by organic farmers that support their key belief "biodiversity furthers health of crop lands".

Bio-diversification of life started to occur almost 3 billion years ago. Since then new species have been evolving and then disappearing en masse from earth.
(a) How many episodes of mass extinctions of species have already taken place and which one is in progress in the current era ?
(b) How is current episode in progress different from the previous episodes and why ? Explain.

(i) Name three molecular diagnostic techniques for diagnosis of a disease.
(ii) List three advantages of molecular diagnostic techniques over conventional method of diagnosis.
Enumerate the main sources of bio-fertilisers giving one example of each.

questions.context: To save the crop plant from the attack of various insect pests the biotechnologists have developed many pest resistant plants. One such example is Bt corn plant. In this plant 'cry' genes were introduced which produces cry-proteins in the plant that has toxic effect on the pest (corn borer). Thus saves the corn plant from the attack of the corn borer. An experimental field study was conducted by the scientists to see the efficacy of the Bt corn plant against the attack of corn borers. Three different species of corn borers namely 'A', 'B', 'C' were collected and were independently fed on non Bt corn plants and Bt corn plants separately for the same period. The extent of the damage caused to the leaf area of the plant was observed and noted down. With the help of the observations and data collected the following bar graph was plotted. Study the graph and answer the questions that follow.
questions.stem: Identify the species of the corn borer that was most successfully controlled by Bt corn plant. Give appropriate reason for your inference.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a bar graph of % of leaf area damaged / mm² (y, 0 to 80) for two groups, Non-Bt Crop and Bt Crop, each with one bar per corn-borer species keyed 'Key for Sps. of corn borers' A (diagonal hatching), B (vertical lines) and C (open); the bar heights decide which species is best controlled, so they are withheld here. Page idx 8.

questions.subtopic: Isolation, Cutting and Amplification of DNA
questions.stem: A gene was identified in a fungus by a research worker in a lab which was considered to be of a great importance in the field of agriculture. As a student of biotechnology, write the steps you would suggest to (i) Isolate this gene of interest from the fungus and (ii) amplify this gene for further experimentation and research.
